transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-02
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alice Moran (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CISO, Argent Health), Carlos Vega (Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Legal)

[00:00] Alice Moran: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Alice from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. with me is Daniel, our SE. we wanted to run through Argent's security posture questions and make sure we cover hosted vs dedicated vs private options.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Perfect, thanks. i'll be leading on security. high-level requirement is HIPAA-covered PHI use, so SOC 2 plus ISO alignment is table stakes, and we have some legal questions too.
[00:30] Daniel Cho: great, quick agenda: SOC 2 / ISO evidence, SSO and provisioning, RBAC and audit logs, encryption and KMS, and deployment/networking for private or dedicated. i'll try to be pragmatic, sorry if i jump between topics.
[00:45] Carlos Vega: sounds good - for context, we run data pipelines in GCP, use internal KMS for some keys, and want to understand if we can bring our own keys or whether we need Redwood-managed KMS. also network: we want VPC peering or private link, not public endpoints.
[01:05] Alice Moran: totally. quick note on compliance: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have an ISO 27001 summary; i will share the full SOC report under NDA after this call.
[01:18] Priya Nair: from legal, we need to see retention windows, audit log granularity, and a sample DPA. also need clarity on data residency - whether data is stored in-region.
[01:32] Daniel Cho: on keys - we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (GCP Cloud KMS/AWS KMS) for Private deployments and Dedicated in most cases; for hosted we offer an option for CMKs with some constraints - i can walk through the integration patterns.
[01:48] Maya Patel: that sounds promising. do you support HSM-backed keys? our security team requires HSM-backed key material for certain workflows.
[02:00] Daniel Cho: yes, we integrate with customer HSM-backed KMS providers; you'll want to run an integration test in the proof-of-concept or private deployment. for hosted we have a flow to use customer KMS via KMS proxy; there are some limitations on rotation windows which i'll document.
[02:19] Alice Moran: i'll include a note in the follow-up with the exact limitations and a playbook.
[02:24] Carlos Vega: what's the story for audit logs? we need immutable logs with retention of 7 years for some data types.
[02:33] Daniel Cho: Redwood Console provides per-request audit logs; retention is configurable for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has a standard retention (90 days) but enterprise add-ons can extend. logs can be exported to your SIEM (Splunk, BigQuery). the logs include request metadata, model id, token counts, and caller identity. note: some fields are redacted in hosted exports by default.
[02:59] Maya Patel: redaction: we're worried about PHI appearing in logs - can you redact or avoid storing transcript bodies in logs?
[03:09] Daniel Cho: yes, we have controls. by default, full request payload is logged for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we offer configurable redaction policies and an option to not persist full payloads. we also support real-time streaming of audit events to customer cloud buckets for archiving.
[03:28] Priya Nair: good. SSO - we use Okta and SCIM for user provisioning. what's your SAML/SCIM coverage?
[03:37] Alice Moran: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user accounts and RBAC. we map SAML groups to roles; SE can show mapping examples.
[03:45] Daniel Cho: yeah, we have a SCIM connector for Okta that provisions teams and role membership. you can choose predefined roles or create custom roles. admin roles, dev roles, read-only auditor role, etc. audit events surface role changes.
[03:59] Carlos Vega: are there RBAC primitives for model-level permissions? we'd like to restrict access to certain high-sensitivity models and limit who can deploy.
[04:09] Daniel Cho: yes, role-based access can be scoped to routes, models, and environment (prod/staging). model-level ACLs are supported in Dedicated and Private with finer-grained enforcement; hosted also supports it but may require an enterprise plan.
[04:23] Maya Patel: Encryption in transit - TLS is a given, but do you do mutual TLS for private endpoints?
[04:30] Daniel Cho: mutual TLS is available for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can enable mTLS per customer network config. for hosted, we use standard TLS with region-specific endpoints and optional private networking via partner private link.
[04:46] Carlos Vega: latency vs cost - our app is latency-sensitive but cost-conscious. how does Dedicated compare vs Hosted?
[04:54] Alice Moran: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, consistent latency and throughput, and isolation. hosted is more elastic but shared, so you trade off some predictability for scale. Private is best when you need full network control, data isolation, and custom KMS/HSM. we'll provide a capacity template in follow up.
[05:15] Priya Nair: on the SOC2 report, what subservice orgs or third-party controls do you rely on? we need a list for our vendor assessment.
[05:24] Alice Moran: we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report and a third-party controls matrix (cloud provider compliance, KMS providers). that will be in the follow-up package.
[05:36] Maya Patel: data residency: can you lock storage to a region? our PHI must reside in US-only regions.
[05:44] Daniel Cho: yes - Dedicated and Private let you pin regions; hosted can be region-locked for enterprise customers. we store model artifacts and logs in-region when requested. i'll detail the region controls in the follow up.
[05:58] Carlos Vega: interesting - database encryption? does Redwood store any decryption keys?
[06:05] Daniel Cho: with customer-managed KMS, the customer controls the key material; Redwood never has plaintext access to CMK-protected secrets. we also support envelope encryption patterns. for hosted with Redwood-managed keys, obviously we manage the keys but we keep them in provider KMS and have strict access controls.
[06:27] Maya Patel: can you speak to redwood's internal access controls? who in Redwood can access customer data for support or debugging?
[06:35] Alice Moran: support access is role-based and audited. we have break-glass procedures for escalations that are logged and require approval. we'll include the access control and admin sudo process in the follow-up.
[06:50] Priya Nair: any penetration testing or external assessments that we can see?
[06:55] Daniel Cho: yes, we have annual third-party pen tests and internal vuln scanning; summary reports are available under NDA.
[07:05] Maya Patel: good. on retention policies, we need flexible retention by data type - conversation logs for training must be deletable within 30 days unless proactively retained.
[07:16] Daniel Cho: we support retention policies per-route and per-customer. Dedicated/Private gives you full control; for hosted we provide retention configuration and deletion APIs, although full deletion in backups may have a longer window - we will document exact SLAs.
[07:35] Carlos Vega: about PII/PHI minimization, do you offer in-line redaction or client-side tokenization?
[07:43] Daniel Cho: Redwood supports pre-processing hooks and client-side redaction in our SDKs; you can also use prefix filters and automatic redaction rules in Dedicated/Private. we'll share examples.
[07:58] Alice Moran: quick timeline Q: what's your intended procurement timeline? helps prioritize getting SOC evidence and pricing.
[08:05] Maya Patel: we're aiming for a vendor decision in Q3, procurement approvals in late July. need security docs and a pilot by June end ideally.
[08:16] Alice Moran: ok we'll try to accelerate the SOC report and get the SE deep dive scheduled this week.
[08:22] [longer section omitted in transcript generator - discussion of pilot scope, sample traffic patterns and compliance questionnaire - summarizing]
[28:40] Daniel Cho: to summarize technical risks: for hosted there's some limitations around CMK rotation and certain HSM features. Dedicated and Private remove most limitations but require more integration work and networking setup.
[28:58] Maya Patel: that's helpful. for scoping the pilot we'd like a small dedicated instance with VPC peering, CMK integration, and log exports to our BigQuery project.
[29:10] Daniel Cho: that's straightforward; we'll include a network diagram and steps for granting the Redwood service account export permissions.
[29:20] Priya Nair: legal ask: sample DPA with breach notification timelines and subcontractor list.
[29:28] Alice Moran: we'll share our standard DPA and a subcontractor list.
[29:34] Carlos Vega: one more - does Redwood support field-level encryption or tokenization for specific PII fields?
[29:41] Daniel Cho: we have support for field-level encryption patterns via the SDKs and we can recommend a pattern using envelope encryption and your KMS. for high-assurance flows we can do client-side crypto.
[29:56] Maya Patel: ok that covers most. anything else from Redwood?
[30:01] Alice Moran: i think we're good. next steps: i'll share SOC2 and DPA; Daniel will produce VPC diagram + KMS notes and we'll propose Dedicated pricing.
[30:12] Maya Patel: thanks, please mark action items and we'll sync next week.
[30:18] Alice Moran: noted. thanks everyone.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings of acronyms (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache") and some run-on sentences.
